<ol>, easy, and <sa>, feel, written as one word: find something easy to do
<ol>, easy, with the causative <sak>; make a thing easy to get, as common as stones
<ol>, easy, with <tak> making an adverb; {oltak a nuntakna} is a life of ease, rest
<oltak>, easily, with the adverb suffix <in>: without effort of one’s own, as when building on work that another has begun
Christian in Rome greeted by Paul at the end of his letter to the Romans
the Olympic Games, the international sports competition
<ol>, easy, with <zaw>, more: easier, or lighter to bear; used after <sangin>, than
exist, be present, be in a place or in a state; {a om} is there is, {om lo} is there is not
come to be, come into existence or come upon someone, often with <hong> or <pah>
in instructions {om ding hi}, there is to be, stands where the English says make
of an event such as war, famine or mourning: take place, there is
stay or live in a person or a place, remain there
<om> written with a capital, at the start of a sentence or in the name {Kumpi Gam Om Lo}, No Kingdom There
<om>, stay, and <hithiat>, at ease: stay still and quiet, doing nothing and not stirring; often a piece of advice, with <in> or <ding> after it, and with <daitak>, quietly, before it
<om>, be or there is, and the linking <a> written as one word: there is, and; it ends a clause and joins it to the next
<om>, be, and the linking <aa>, and, written as one word: there is or there are, and
a country on the Arabian Peninsula
son of Eliphaz and grandson of Esau, a chief of Edom
<om> and <bang> written as one word: as there is, in keeping with what exists; <thukhun ombang in> is according to the law in force
<om> and <bangin> written as one word: as there is, in keeping with what exists; {thukhun ombangin} is according to the law in force

terms: there are more/be in addition/be added
definition: <om>, be, with <beh>, here in addition, written as one word: there is more of something besides what there was; {ombeh lai} is there are still more
<om>, be, and <ciang>, when, written as one word: when there is, when one is in a place; {ih omciang} is when we are
<om>, be, and <cih>, that, written as one word: that there is or that it is so, before a verb of saying
<om>, be, with <cip>, firmly: stay as one is without moving, answering or changing
<omcip>, stay in place, and <den>, always, written as one word: stay there or remain so all the time
<omcip>, stay still, with the linking suffix <in>: remaining without a move or a word, and
<omcip>, stay without moving, with the noun suffix: a staying in one place, as staying indoors, or the place where one always stays
<omcip>, stay still, with the causative <sak>: make people stay where they are and not leave, as in a lockdown
<om>, be, with the emphatic <citciat> written as one word: it is plainly there, there is indeed
<om>, be, with <dan>, manner: how a person or a people live and behave; also how someone is getting on
<omdan>, way of being, and <khawldan>, way of staying: a pair that names as one thing how a person lives and behaves among others
plural of <omdan>: how things are, or how a person lives and behaves
<om>, be, with <den>, continually: go on being so, stay as it is
<om> and <ding> written as one word: there will be, will be held; also is to stay
<omding> with the linking <a> written as one word: there will be, and; before a noun, that is to be
<om> and <dinghi> written as one word: there will be; after a number, there are thought to be about that many
<om> and <dingin> written as one word: so as to be, or as likely to be; with <ki ummawh>, be suspected to be, and with <um>, believe that there will be
last letter of the Greek alphabet, used with Alpha as a title of God and of Christ, the beginning and the end
<om>, be, with <gawp>, severely or to excess: be present and behave grossly
<om> and <gige> written as one word: is there all the time, there always is
<om> and <hang> written as one word: on account of there being, or although one is; at the end of a sentence also there are, said of us

terms: there is none at all/not be at all
definition: <om>, be, and <hetlo>, not at all, written as one word: there is none at all, be not there at all
<om>, be there, and the sentence-final <hi> written as one word: closes a statement that something or someone is there
<om>, be, with the question particle <hiam>, written as one word: is there, what is there, how is it
<om> and <hiding> written as one word: there must be or there probably is, said of what is supposed and not known for sure
<om> and <hithiat> written as one word: stay quietly and undisturbed, without care or concern
<om>, be, and <huai>, worthy of, written as one word: that ought to be there, that deserves to exist or to stay
<om>, be or stay, with the linking suffix <in>, joining it to the next clause

terms: be here and there/occur in many places
definition: <om>, be, and <kawikawi>, here and there, written as one word: be found in many places, be all around
<om> and the negative <kei> written as one word: there is none, is not there; <omkei leh> is if there is none, without

terms: without/if there is no/were it not for
definition: <omkei>, there is not, and <leh>, here if: placed after a noun, if there is none of it, without it; the result follows

terms: if there is no/if there were not/without
definition: <om> and <keileh> written as one word: if there is not, if someone or something does not exist

terms: happen to be/be there by chance
definition: <om>, be, with <kha>, by chance: happen to be somewhere; with <ding> or <thei>, there may be

terms: there may be/there will probably be
definition: <omkha>, happen to be, with <ding>, will, written as one word: there may well be, there are likely to be

terms: is there by any chance/are there perhaps
definition: <om>, be, with <khahiam>, by any chance, written as one word: a question whether someone or something happens to be there
form of <omkha> used before <leh>, <loh> and <pen>: be or exist by chance, mostly in if-clauses and warnings

terms: if there happens to be/if there should be
definition: <omkha>, happen to be, and <leh>, here if, written as one word: if there should be any
<omkha> and <lo> written as one word: there happened to be none, no one was there, often of people killed or hurt
<om>, be, and <khathei>, perhaps, written as one word: there may well be, it could happen
<om>, be, with <khawm>, together: be, stay or live with someone; <tawh> marks the companion
<omkhawm> with the linking ending <in>: being together with someone, <tawh> marks the companion
<omkhawm>, be together, with the noun suffix <na>

terms: cause to be with/put together with
definition: <omkhawm>, be together, with <sak>, cause: make or let someone be in the same place as others
<omkhawm>, be together, with plural {-te}: those who are with someone

terms: can live together/be able to stay together
definition: <omkhawm> and <thei> written as one word: be able to be or live together
<om>, be, with <khin>, already: have been somewhere or in a state up to now, be there already
<om> and <khinta> written as one word: there is already, has already come to be in a place or state

terms: have already been/there have already been
definition: <om> and <khinzo> written as one word: has already come to be, there has already been
<om>, be or stay, with <khit>, finished; mostly as {omkhit ciangin}, after being or staying
<omkhit>, have been, with the noun suffix <na>: the fact of having been something for a time
<om>, be, with <khol>, beforehand: be in readiness for what is to be done
<om> and <khollo> written as one word: there is hardly any, there are not many

form of <omkhawm> used before <loh>, <ding>, <theih> and <nading>
polite word for sexual intercourse, mostly of husband and wife, as in {nupa omkhop}; the plain sense is only being in one place together
<omkhop> and <ding> written as one word: to be together as husband and wife, to sleep together
<omkhop>, be together, with the noun suffix <na>
a polite word for sexual intercourse, after <nupa>, husband and wife, or <numei pasal>, woman and man; after <mipi> or <mihon>, crowd, it stays the plain being together of sense 1

terms: permission to stay/right to remain/leave to stay
definition: <om>, stay, and <khuan>, permission, written as one word: leave given by an authority to stay in a place or country; {omkhuan pia} is allow to stay

terms: there are some/occur now and then
definition: <om> and <kiaukiau> written as one word: there are some here and there, it happens now and then
<om> be with <kik>, again or back: return to an earlier state; with <lo>, be no more

terms: will be again/will be held again
definition: <omkik>, be again, and <ding> written as one word: there will again be, it will take place again
<om>, be, with <kim>, complete: all are there, or be present throughout a place
<om>, be, with <lai>, still: still be there, be left; {a omlai} is the rest, what remains
poetic word for <natna>, used in songs; not the verb remain

terms: will still be/there are probably still
definition: <omlai>, still be there, with <ding>, will, written as one word: there will still be, there are thought to be more

<omlai>, remain, with <pi>; {omlaipi mahin} is even while it was still there
<omlai>, remain, with <sun>: still left; {a omlaisun teng} or {a omlaisun khempeuh} is all who are still left, the remnant
<om> and <laitak> written as one word: while being or staying, be in a place or busy with something at that moment
<omlai>, remain, with plural <te>: the people or things that are left; in Kings, the remaining acts of a reign
<omlai>, remain, with <teng>, all: everyone or everything that is still left
after a noun and <a>, for as long as that thing still exists

terms: among those that exist/among the ones there are
definition: <om> and <lak> written as one word, after <a> and before <pan> or <ah>: from among the things that there are

<om>, be, and <leh>, if, written as one word: if there is, if someone is in a place
<om> and <lel>, merely, written as one word: there simply is, just be or stay there
<om>, be or stay, and <leng>, if, written as one word: if I or we stay, if we had
<om> and <leuleu> written as one word: there is once more, or there is on the other hand; closes a report of another event of the same kind
<om>, be, with <lian>, here exactly, written as one word: be exactly there, exist for certain; {omlian nailo} is there is not yet a definite one

terms: there is no definite/not exactly exist
definition: <omlian>, be definite, and <lo>, not, written as one word: there is nothing definite or exact
<om>, be, with <lo>, not: where something is not present, as {mi omlo}, without people, and {silngo-omlo}, without yeast, unleavened

terms: there will not be/will not be
definition: <om>, be, <lo>, not, and <ding>, will, written as one word: there will be none, will not be; as an instruction, must not stay

<om>, be, with <loh>, not, and the noun suffix <na>: the fact that there is none
<om>, be there, and <loin>, without, written as one word: without there being any, with none

terms: there is none/turn out not to be there
definition: <omlo>, not being there, with <mawk>, here marking what is unexpected or simply so, written as one word: there is simply none, or someone is found not to be there
<omlo>, there is not, and <pah> written as one word: there is none either, said as the plain result of what was stated before
<om>, be, with <lo>, not; {thu omlopi-a} is when there is no matter, for no reason

terms: those who are not there/those not in
definition: <om>, be, and <lote>, those who are not, written as one word: the people or things that are not in a place, a list or a state

<om> and <lua> written as one word: there is very much or very many of something; with a negative, there is not so very much

terms: before there was/before the existence of

<om>, be or stay, and the particle <mai>, just, written as one word: there simply are, just stay around

terms: be there for a time/happen to occur
definition: <om> and <man> written as one word: there has been, something was there or came about for a time

terms: there seems to be none/hardly exist

<om>, be, with <mun>, often; {ommun lo} is be rare

terms: place to stay/for staying/so that there may be

<om>, be, with <nai>, yet; in a question: is there any so far

terms: there is not yet/not exist yet
definition: <om> and <nailo> written as one word: there is none so far, has not yet come about
<omna>, the place where someone or something is, and <lam>, direction, written as one word: the side on which it is, usually followed by <ah>
<om> and <napi> written as one word: although there is, or although someone is there, often followed by <in>

<omna>, the place where someone or something is, with <teng>, all, written as one word: the whole place, or all the places, where it is
<om>, be, with <nawn>, any more or further

terms: there is no longer/be no more/no longer exist

terms: will no longer be/will be no more
definition: <om>, be, and <nawnloding> written as one word: there will no longer be, will not exist any more

<omngei>, have once been, with <lo>, not, written as one word: there has never been, it has never happened before

terms: former residence/place where one has been
definition: <omngei>, have been, with the noun suffix <na>: the place where someone once lived or stayed; also where or how something has always been
<om>, be, with the expressive <ngeingai>, written as one word: many people are there in a stir or commotion
<om>, be, with <nop>, form of <nuam>, want
<omnop>, want to be, with the noun suffix <na>
<om>, be, with <nuam>, want
<om>, be, with <nuam>, pleasant: of a person who is pleasant to be with; the English has fine-looking

terms: tend to occur/be liable to happen/be common

doubled form of <om>, be, for a state that continues, often followed by <lai>, still
<omom>, go on being, with <in>; {a omomin ngaihsun} is think that he is still there
<omom> with the noun suffix <na>, after a person marker: the place where each one is living; {i omomna ah} is wherever we are

terms: he who is/the one who is
definition: <om> be, with <pa> marking a man: the one who is in a place or with someone

<om>, be, with <pak>, for a short while

<om>, be there, with <pan>, here only just, written as one word and used with <bek>, only: there is no more than that so far

<ompih> with the linking ending <in>: being with someone to help and support
<ompih>, be with, with <lai>, still
<ompih>, be with, with the noun suffix <na>: someone’s being with a person, especially the presence of God
<ompihna> written with a capital in {Ompihna Anlum}, the bread of the Presence that is set before God

<om>, be, with <sa>, already: that which already is or was there before; {thu omsa bangin} is according to the word already given, {ngeina kip omsa} is the established rule
<om>, be, with <sak>, cause: cause to be somewhere, put
set or keep someone or something in a place, let remain there
make something exist or arise, not put it in a place: the object is a state or an event, as {buaina omsak}, cause trouble, and {kimuanna omsak lo}, create no trust
<omsak>, cause to be, with the linking suffix <in>
<omsak> with <kik>, again: cause to be as before, put back in its place; {ki-omsakkik} is the passive
<omsak>, let be, with <lai>, still: leave a thing as it is for a while longer

terms: not allow/not let there be/not cause

<omsak>, make be, with <zo>, be able; {nuamtakin omsakzo} is keep in peace
<om>, be, with the particle <sam>, indeed, to be sure: there certainly is or are, often granting a point before a contrast

terms: there is none/not be at all
definition: <om>, be, with <samlo>, not at all, written as one word: there is none after all, there was not any
<om>, stay, with <san>, here leaving something aside: stay as one is and do nothing about a matter; {a thei lo bangin omsan} is carry on as if one did not know
<omsa> already existing, with the plural <te>; after a noun it describes it, as {pawlpi omsate}, the churches already there
<om>, be or stay, with <sawm>, intend
<om>, be, and <sawnsawn> written as one word: there is, with the sense that this too is the case or goes on being so
<om> and <selo> written as one word: there is none to speak of, without there being any such thing

terms: there is none at all/not be at all
definition: <om>, be, and <seselo>, not at all, written as one word: there is no such thing at all, or it is not in that place at all
<om>, be, with <suak>, onward: go on being in the same place or state, stay on
<omsuak>, remain, with <in> linking it to what follows
<omsuak>, stay on, with the noun suffix <na>
<omsuak>, stay on, with <suak> said twice, written as one word: go on staying, as in a country after the visa has run out
<omsuak>, stay on, with plural <te>
the only one or the little that there is, like <neihsun> for what one has; {omsun teng} is all that there is
<om>, be, with <sung>, within or during: the time while someone is in a place; {ka omsung khempeuh} is all the time I was there

terms: what little there is/the few there are
definition: <om>, be, and <sunsun>, what little, written as one word: the little that exists, the few who are there
<om> be with <ta>, which marks a state that now holds: now is, has come to be; {koi-ah omta ahi hiam} asks where something is now
<om>, be, and <takpi>, truly, written as one word: there really is, really take place
<om> and <taktak> written as one word: there really is, it really happened
<om>, be, and <tawh>, with, written as one word after <a> and before <kibang>: {a omtawh kibang} is it is like being in the place or state named
<om>, be, with plural <te>: those who are in a place or state; {a omte} is the ones who are
particle used in making a comparison
<om> and <teh> written as one word, after <a>: when or whenever there is; compare <takteh>

terms: there is indeed/exist to be sure
definition: <om>, be, with the emphatic <tei> written as one word, used before <hang> or <hangin>: although there indeed is
<om> and <tek> written as one word: each of those named is there, each one has it

terms: all that is/everything in/all who are
definition: <om>, be, with <teng>, all: all that there is in a place, all who are there
<om>, be, with <thei>, can: can be, be able to stay as it is

terms: may be/may happen/will be able to be
definition: <omthei>, can be, and <ding>, will, written as one word: there may be, it may happen, one will be able to be so
form of <omthei>, can be, used before <nading>; {a omtheih nadingin} is so that it may be
<omtheih>, be able to be, with {-na}: being allowed to stay in a country, as in {omtheihna permit}; also a place where something can be
<om>, be, with <theilo>, unable, written as one word: cannot be there, cannot take place, there cannot be

terms: can even be/may well be/happen to be
definition: <omthei> and <mawk> written as one word: there can indeed be, said with surprise or disapproval of something that does occur

terms: can no longer be/be no longer possible
definition: <omthei>, can be, and <nawnlo>, no longer, written as one word: there can no longer be, it can no longer exist

terms: happen now and then/tend to occur/there are often
definition: <omthei>, can be, and <zel>, repeatedly, written as one word: it happens from time to time, there tend to be
<om>, be, and <thu>, matter, written as one word after <a>: {sunglam a omthu} is what is inside a person, the state of the inner life
<om>, be, with <to>, up or onward; be high above a thing, and of time, go on being in a place
form of <omto>, be up on, used before <ciangin>, when
<om>, be there, with <tuak>, here showing what the writer supposes, written as one word: there seems to be, there surely is
<om>, be or live, with <tuak>, each or both, written as one word: both are, each of them is

terms: seem not to be/there is apparently no
definition: <omtuak>, there seems to be, and <lo>, not, written as one word: as far as can be seen there is none, there is no sign of it
<om>, be, with <tual>; in the verse the wise keep among mourning and fools among pleasure
<om>, be, with <tuam>, separate; {hun omtuam lo} is there is no separate time
<om>, be there, and <tuan> written as one word, nearly always before a negative or in a question: there is not really any, there is no such thing after all

terms: there is none/not be at all
definition: <om> be, <tuan> and the negative <lo> written as one word: there is none after all, nothing of the kind exists
<om>, be, and the plural marker <uh> written as one word: they are, they stay or remain so

terms: appear suddenly/be there all at once
definition: <om>, be, with <vat>, suddenly
<om>, be, and the emphatic <vet> written as one word before a negative: there is none at all, not be there at all

name of two men: a son of Jahdai in the family of Caleb of Judah, and a son of Azmaveth, a warrior of Benjamin who joined David at Ziklag
name of two men, a descendant of Jerahmeel of Judah and the father of On of Reuben; {Peleth mite} are the Pelethites, the bodyguard of David led by Benaiah
keep away from something bad or dangerous, or get out of its way; {siatna pelh} is shun evil
fail to keep a promise or covenant; with a negative, {pelh lo}, without fail or unfailingly
<pelh>, avoid, and <ding>, to, written as one word: what is to be avoided, should keep away from
be absent from a counted number; also written <peelhem>
